summary: Fixed the no-RoPE MLA KV scatter path so DCP-widened virtual locations are owner-filtered and divided by the DCP width before indexing a per-rank buffer. The same path now honors reserved_skip_index. This restores the DCP contract already implemented by the RoPE branch and prevents writes beyond physical per-rank capacity.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before run on the base implementation: both DCP rank cases wrote raw virtual rows instead of localized physical rows, including rows beyond the simulated per-rank capacity; the no-RoPE path also overwrote the reserved slot. Raw output: reports/j-2205162890bd/raw/failing_before_norope_dcp.txt

Passing-after GPU regression: owner filtering and virtual-to-physical localization passed for DCP ranks 0 and 1, and reserved-index skipping passed (3 tests). Raw output: reports/j-2205162890bd/raw/passing_after_norope_dcp.txt
Existing and new MLA buffer GPU coverage: 8 passed and 58 NVIDIA TMA-only cases skipped on ROCm. Raw output: reports/j-2205162890bd/raw/full_mla_buffer_suite.txt

gpu_execution.evidence: Tests executed Triton kernels on the assigned AMD Instinct MI350X (gfx950) through torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2. The regression compared complete GPU buffer contents against independently constructed owner/localization expectations.

remaining_limitations: The reported end-to-end workload requires 8 NVIDIA B200 GPUs, CUDA/FlashInfer TRT-LLM MLA, and GLM-5.3 weights. The prepared environment has one AMD Instinct MI350X (gfx950) and no model weights, so the full model, B200-specific backend execution, TP8/DCP8 communication, HiCache interaction, and long-context serving reproduction remain unverified.
The deterministic tiny Llama fixture is not architecture-qualified for GLM-5.3 no-RoPE MLA or distributed DCP, so it was not used as a substitute for the reported workload.
No native library was changed or rebuilt; the defect and correction are in the Python-hosted Triton kernel.
